question: The splitting up of white light into seven components as it enters a glass prism is called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**dispersion of light**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The splitting up of white light into seven components as it enters a glass prism is called **dispersion of light**.
 
• This phenomenon occurs because different colors of light have **different wavelengths **and thus, they refract by different amounts when passing through a medium like glass.
 
• As a result, the white light is separated into its constituent spectral colors: **red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet**, commonly remembered by the acronym **ROYGBIV**.
 
• **Dispersion** is a key concept in the study of optics and is fundamental to understanding how prisms and other optical devices work.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isaac Newton** was the first to demonstrate that white light is composed of different colors using a prism.
 
• This discovery was crucial in the development of the field of spectroscopy, which analyzes the light spectrum to understand the properties of light-emitting substances.
 
• Dispersion is not limited to prisms; it can also be observed in natural phenomena such as rainbows, where water droplets in the atmosphere act as prisms.
 
• In addition to prisms, other devices like **diffraction gratings** can also disperse light into its spectral components.
